html:
October 28, 2026

Netanyahu bloc falls short of majority as Israeli vote count continues

tags: politics, elections
sources: @total.hypocrisy, @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

Israel held national elections on October 27, with exit polls showing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition losing its majority. With 71% of votes counted, his right-wing bloc was projected at 54 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, ahead of Gadi Eisenkot's 47, with Arab parties projected at 19 and positioned as potential kingmakers. Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister while coalition talks begin, and Israeli markets slid on the deadlock. Results must be certified within eight days, placing final certification around November 4, and Netanyahu has alleged without evidence that the vote was rigged. Likud and Eisenkot's Yashar! party both oppose Palestinian statehood but differ on Haredi conscription, the powers of the Supreme Court, and whether a state commission should investigate the October 7 failures.

US grants visas to Flavio Bolsonaro after Brazilian election defeat

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

The State Department has granted visas to Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family after he lost Brazil's presidential runoff to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva by nearly four percentage points on October 25. Bolsonaro travelled to the United States and has arrived in Miami, departing as a Brazilian Supreme Court deadline to surrender his passports approached and while he faces corruption and money laundering investigations. He has refused to concede and accused election officials of fraud without evidence; President Trump also called the election rigged without evidence. Members of Brazil's legislature are calling for Interpol to issue a red notice, and his brother Eduardo, who lives in Texas, faces an arrest warrant after a four-year sentence for illegally lobbying the Trump administration. Their father, Jair Bolsonaro, is serving a lengthy prison term in Brazil over an attempted coup.

Brazil opens police investigation into donor network co-founded by JD Vance

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A Brazilian Supreme Court justice has requested a police investigation into Rockbridge, a donor network co-founded by US Vice President JD Vance, over possible interference in Brazil's election. The inquiry will examine whether the network provided assistance to defeated right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro. Foreign donations to Brazilian elections are illegal under Brazilian law.

Hacker targets Federal Election Commission a week before midterms

tags: politics, surveillance
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

The Federal Election Commission temporarily shut down its web-facing services after an attempted breach, according to Reuters. The electronic filing system used by campaigns and political groups to report fundraising and spending has been offline, reducing disclosure ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. The identity and motive of the attacker are not known, and the FBI has not determined who was responsible. The FEC does not operate polling places.

Study estimates Utah data center could cause 45 premature deaths a year

tags: tech, health, climate
sources: @carolinegleich

The first health study of the Stratos data center in Box Elder County, Utah, commissioned by the NRDC from EmPower Analytics Group and released October 26, 2026, finds that at full build-out the project would require roughly twice the electricity all Utah power plants generated in 2024. If that power comes from gas, the study's highest estimate is 45 premature deaths and up to $690 million in health costs annually, along with increased asthma attacks and hospital visits. Box Elder and Cache counties would be hit hardest, with pollution reaching the whole Wasatch Front and into Idaho, Wyoming and Colorado. The developers have not said how the facility will be powered; Utah Clean Energy says regulators should count these health costs before deciding.

Pentagon drafts plan for bases to operate independently for 90 days

tags: defence, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

The Pentagon is updating contingency planning for a global conflict that knocks out power grids, cripples supply chains and cuts military bases off from essential services. Under the initiative, reported as "Fortress," every major US military installation would prepare to operate independently for at least 90 days, with portable nuclear reactors, backup power, and reserves of ammunition, critical minerals, medical supplies and jam-resistant communications. Officials cite Chinese pre-positioning of malware in US critical infrastructure. The plan is expected to cost billions of dollars across nearly 200 installations. The UK and Japan are urging households to prepare for three days without essential services, and Germany is advising ten days of food and water over potential Russian sabotage.

Trump administration to restart wage garnishment for defaulted student loans

tags: economy, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Trump administration is preparing to resume aggressive collection on defaulted federal student loans, according to Forbes, affecting nearly 10 million borrowers. The Treasury Department is partnering with the Department of Education to seize wages, benefits and tax refunds in the coming weeks and months, restarting collections that were paused under President Biden. Borrowers subject to garnishment receive a notice prior to wage withholding, a 30-day warning, and can request a hearing on grounds of extreme financial hardship.

James O'Keefe charged with unlawful voting and identity theft in Minnesota

tags: legal, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty has charged conservative activist James O'Keefe and influencer Cam Higbee with felony counts of unlawful voting and identity theft, according to NBC News. Prosecutors allege the pair entered polling places during Minnesota's state primary voting on August 11 and identified themselves using the names of registered voters in those precincts without the voters' knowledge or permission.

Hegseth orders creation of four-star autonomous warfare command

tags: defence, tech
sources: @oafnation_actual

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has ordered the establishment of a new four-star Autonomous Warfare Command by October 1, 2027, according to The Center Square. The command would lead joint unmanned and autonomous warfare with its own personnel, budget and purchasing authority. The Pentagon has not disclosed the cost, though officials said $54 billion is being sought for autonomous systems. An action plan is due Friday.

Trump says ending Iran conflict is a question of timing

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Speaking about Iran, President Trump said the United States is "in a very good position" and that continuing the conflict is simply a question of when he wants to end it. He said Iran wants to make a deal but has been stringing the process along, suggesting they may be waiting for the election. He added that the election would not help them.

China to send special envoy to Middle East over widening conflict

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

China will dispatch a special envoy to the Middle East soon, Beijing said Tuesday. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said China is highly concerned about the conflict spilling into the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea, according to Reuters. The envoy will push dialogue aimed at easing tensions and preventing further deterioration. Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials met Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday.

Drones shot down near US embassy in Baghdad's Green Zone

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

US embassy air defenses engaged drones near Baghdad's Green Zone on Tuesday, according to Reuters. Iraq's Security Media Cell said one drone was downed near the district, while security sources said embassy defenses engaged two drones at the perimeter. Debris was recovered at two sites and the origin of the drones is under investigation.

CENTCOM denies Iranian claim that US forces left Strait of Hormuz

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

US Central Command pushed back Tuesday on an Iranian claim that American forces had abandoned the Strait of Hormuz, calling it false. The command said US forces remain present and vigilant in the strait and pointed to Adm. Brad Cooper's weekend flight over the waterway. The rebuttal responds to an October 23 assertion by the IRGC Navy commander that US ships had moved hundreds of kilometers away.

Explosions hit Kyiv again as localized ceasefire begins near Oleshky

tags: war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Explosions were heard in Kyiv on Tuesday morning, a day after a Russian strike on the capital killed at least one person and injured ten, according to a Reuters witness. Strikes also hit Kharkiv and Pavlohrad on Monday. The new blasts came as a localized ceasefire took effect around Russian-held Oleshky to allow aid deliveries and evacuations.

Finland and Norway break Western freeze on direct contact with Putin

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The presidents of Finland and Norway called Vladimir Putin on Tuesday to press for an end to the war in Ukraine, breaking a Western freeze on direct contact, according to Reuters. Finnish President Alexander Stubb described the conversation as "frank and substantive," while Norway's Jonas Gahr Store emphasized de-escalation. The Kremlin signaled no compromise, saying peace requires that Russia's interests be taken into account.

Democrats lead generic congressional ballot by eight points

tags: politics, elections
sources: @oafnation_actual

Democrats lead Republicans by 8 points among likely voters on the generic congressional ballot, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. President Trump's approval rating stands at 40 percent. One in three Americans report financial hardship and four in ten say their personal finances have worsened. NPR reports Democrats are favored to take the House while the Senate remains a toss-up.

Court rules against Trump administration over taxpayer-funded campaign ads

tags: legal, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

The Trump administration lost a lawsuit brought by the organization Common Cause over the use of taxpayer money to run federal campaign advertising. Common Cause sued on the grounds that public funds were being spent on partisan political ads and prevailed in the case.

US ambassador tells Canadian business leaders Ottawa may be blamed for midterm losses

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

The US Ambassador to Canada told a closed-door meeting of business leaders on Tuesday that Ottawa could be blamed if key midterm races go against President Trump, according to CTV News. He cited the Maine contest between Troy Jackson and Susan Collins and the Michigan race between Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers. The ambassador said dealing with Trump would become more difficult for Canada as a result, against a backdrop of continuing US tariffs and trade disputes.

Experts warn NOAA cuts leave US exposed during record El Niño

tags: climate, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Experts speaking to The Guardian warn the United States faces a "cascade of dangers" during an unprecedented El Niño event, worsened by sweeping cuts to NOAA under the Trump administration that have hampered forecasting and extreme-weather response. Projected effects include sea level rise of up to a foot around California, debris flows, landslides, flash floods, supercharged storms in the American West and rising surface temperatures. Scientists say the forecasting and response system is untested in its current state. The effects of the event are already being felt globally.

Iraqi court sentences six French nationals to life for Islamic State membership

tags: legal, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

An Iraqi court sentenced six French nationals to life in prison on Tuesday for membership of the Islamic State, according to Reuters. A seventh man, aged 23, received 15 years. The judge said the court chose life terms over the death penalty because the defendants were young. The men were among 47 French suspects transferred from Syria to Iraq last year, and their lawyer said the group will appeal.

Serbian state broadcaster apologizes for years of pro-government coverage

tags: media, politics
sources: @groundnews

Radio Television Vojvodina, a Serbian state broadcaster, apologized on air for years of favorable coverage of President Aleksandar Vucic after his party's defeat by the student-led opposition in Sunday's parliamentary election. "For years, we failed to fulfil our duty," news anchor Goran Eror told viewers, and the station's acting editor-in-chief resigned as students demanded the removal of senior officials over political bias. The Student List secured 52.8% of votes, enough to govern without coalition partners, ending 12 years of rule by Vucic's party. The movement grew out of protests following a 2024 railway station collapse that killed 16 people.

North Korean howitzers pointed south draw attention at border observatory

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Three 122-mm self-propelled howitzers with barrels pointed south were visible near Kaepung by Monday, according to a Reuters witness at a South Korean border observatory. Seoul says the weapons are older systems rather than new deployments. Analysts described the display as a show of force rather than a combat upgrade.

Brazilian markets plunge after Lula's re-election

tags: markets, politics
sources: @groundnews

Brazil's Ibovespa index fell roughly 14% to 176,025 points by Tuesday following President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's re-election on October 25, reversing gains built on expectations of a Flavio Bolsonaro win. The selloff triggered trading halts for the first time since 2020, with the index falling as much as 17% during Monday's session and some individual stocks losing more than half their value. Brazil's currency suffered its steepest decline in over two decades. Investors had anticipated spending cuts under Bolsonaro, and Lula's victory raised concerns about continued government spending and a budget deficit exceeding 9% of GDP.

Detroit police kill armed man after hours-long standoff

tags: policing
sources: @oafnation_actual

Detroit police shot and killed a 50-year-old man on Tuesday after an hours-long standoff, according to Police Chief Todd Bettison. Police say the man barricaded himself at home and pointed an assault rifle at officers. No officers were injured, and family members told police the man may have been in a mental health crisis.

Campaigners press for return of carriers still deployed in Iran conflict

tags: war, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Campaigners calling for an end to the conflict in Iran note that several US ships remain deployed as long as or longer than the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has returned home. They say crews aboard those vessels face similar conditions and deserve the same attention and return. The message was circulated alongside calls to end what the campaigners describe as an illegal war in Iran.

Utah voters told mailed ballots must arrive by 8 p.m. on Election Day

tags: elections
sources: @carolinegleich

Utah voters have been advised that it is too late to return ballots by mail, because ballots must be in the clerk's hands by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, and postmarks no longer count. The Postal Service applies its date stamp at a regional sorting center, which can be days after a ballot is dropped in a mailbox. Voters are instructed to use a drop box, sign the envelope and write the last four digits of their Utah driver license, state ID or Social Security number on the back. Voters who lost a ballot can vote in person on Election Day and can register on the spot with ID and proof of address.

Utah endorsement slate urges no votes on Amendments A and B

tags: elections, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

A slate of endorsements for Utah's 2026 general election covers races from Congress and the state legislature to county offices and school boards, along with judicial retention and ballot questions. The recommendations include voting to retain all listed appellate judges while voting against 4th District Court Judge Thomas Low and Weber County Justice Court Judge Trent Nelson. Both Amendment A and Amendment B are opposed; Amendment B would allow a citizen ballot measure to fail even with 59% support while lawmakers need only a simple majority.
